big: Meena has ₹2 lakh of spare money. Rohan says to invest it. Dadi says to pay down the loan. The truth depends on one number: the rate her loan charges.

lines: If I pay extra, will the bank let me, and does it really help?
Yes, on most floating-rate loans to individuals there is no penalty. Every rupee prepaid stops earning interest for the lender.

note: Choose to keep the EMI and shorten the tenure. This saves the most.

alt: Two sets of bars comparing loan years and total repaid with and without a prepayment
caps: Two borrowers with the same loan.
One pays only the EMI and finishes in 20 years.
The other adds ₹2 lakh in year 2 and finishes in 17.3 years.
That one payment saves about ₹6.7 lakh of the total.

q: Rohan prepays ₹1 lakh early in a long loan. What does that do?
opts: Stops interest on that money for years
Raises the interest rate on the rest
Cancels the whole loan right away at once
Has no effect until the final month
why: Money prepaid early no longer earns interest, and early years are the biggest.
Prepaying does not raise the rate. It lowers the amount that interest is charged on.
A part payment lowers the balance, but it does not clear the whole loan.
The effect begins from the next interest period, not at the end.

q: Meena prepays and has to pick: shorter tenure or lower EMI. Which saves more interest?
opts: Lower the EMI and keep the tenure
Both save exactly the same amount
Keep the EMI and shorten the tenure
Neither, since prepayment never saves interest
why: A lower EMI eases the month but leaves more interest to build in later years.
The two choices do not save the same, since one cuts the years.
Keeping the EMI clears the balance faster, so less interest piles up.
Prepayment does save interest, since it lowers the balance.

q: Rohan's friend offers 8.75% against Rohan's 9.5% on a ₹20 lakh, 15-year loan. What should he do first?
opts: Move at once, since a lower rate is always better
Add up all costs, then ask his lender to match
Ignore it, since lenders never change rates
Pay the processing fee without reading the terms
why: A lower rate helps only if the savings are bigger than the costs of moving.
Fees and charges can eat the gain, and his own lender may match the rate.
Offers can be matched, so ignoring the chance is a loss for him.
Paying fees unread is how hidden costs get through.

q: Which number shows the full cost of borrowing, fees included?
opts: The headline rate in the advertisement
The EMI quoted by a friend for his loan
The lender's brand ranking among banks
The APR in the Key Facts Statement
why: A headline rate can leave out fees, so a cheaper-looking loan may cost more.
A friend's EMI is for a different loan, so it tells her nothing here.
Rankings do not show what this particular loan will cost her.
The annual percentage rate adds processing fees and other charges to the interest.

pts: Prepay early, when the balance is high and years remain.
Keep the EMI and shorten the tenure for the biggest saving.
Compare loans by APR and total cost, and ask your lender to match first.
